terms.gloss: a deponent verb, passive in form and active in meaning
evidence: Charis. p. 143; Diom. p. 327; Prisc. p. 787 P. (Lewis & Short s.v. dēpōnō)
terms.comment: The verb that “lays aside” its passive meaning (verbum understood): loquor, sequor, fruor (Traupman 228). The term is the later grammarians’. Quintilian describes such verbs as things we do said patiendī modō, in the passive form (9.3.7).
The grammarians’ term (Gellius, Charisius): a verb passive in form and active in meaning, as hortor, sequor.

phrases.latin: in nātūrā verbōrum est et quae facimus patiendī modō saepe dīcere, ut arbitror, suspicor
phrases.english: it is in the nature of verbs often to say what we do in the passive, as arbitror, suspicor
Give some examples of a deponent verb.

deponens.html: Vowels before ns are long (Cic. Or. 159).
